integration: Pass unique track IDs and stable title, artist, album and duration records. onSelect drives the host selection or player.
Like, queue and removal actions are separate sibling controls; omit callbacks to hide actions the host does not support.
Optional host artwork should be licensed and served reliably. The default cover studies are original, offline-safe illustrations.

block-music-workspace.useWhen: Composing a full listening application with discovery, a searchable collection, a shared queue and persistent playback.
block-music-workspace.avoidWhen: Copying a streaming service brand or publishing an audio catalogue without rights to its media and artwork.
integration: Supply MusicTrack records with licensed src URLs. Selection and playback remain distinct and actual media events govern playing state.
Persist queue and liked-state changes through host observers. Retained views keep the collection, search and player position intact.
The offline demo uses fictional releases and original 12-second audio; it begins muted. Production integrations own licensed assets.

collab-message-list.useWhen: Showing a readable team conversation with reply affordances, reversible reactions and respectful arrival of new posts.
collab-message-list.avoidWhen: Treating a visual conversation as a transport layer or asserting delivery before a host returns an authoritative message.
integration: Pass stable message IDs and author identities. Drive reactions and thread navigation through host callbacks.
The viewport follows own posts and preserves earlier reading positions for incoming posts.
Animate reaction figures in both directions; live announcements apply to added messages rather than every count frame.

block-team-workspace.useWhen: Composing channels and direct-message rooms with persistent drafts, an asynchronous send contract and retained threads.
block-team-workspace.avoidWhen: Publishing a communication application without supplying its transport, user identity and persistence requirements.
integration: Supply channels, people and initialMessages with stable IDs. onSend returns the server’s authoritative channel-scoped message.
Channel drafts and opened threads remain mounted. A late response never clears text edited during the request.
Reactions and thread interactions are session state in the example; hosts own durable storage and realtime transport.

collab-call-stage.useWhen: Presenting real participant video streams with camera-off fallbacks, a spotlight layout and clear host-owned media controls.
collab-call-stage.avoidWhen: Using placeholder portraits or animation to claim a live media connection, active speaker or hardware permission.
integration: Supply participant streams from your own session transport. The stage never acquires a camera or microphone by itself.
Use CallControls separately when controls must remain visible across other application views.
Only supply captions and activeSpeakerId when the host has real data. The host owns track lifetimes and audio routing.

block-meetings-workspace.useWhen: Composing a working meeting application with linked agenda context, persistent room controls and independently retained notes.
block-meetings-workspace.avoidWhen: Treating an interface block as a conferencing transport or declaring a room joined before the host acknowledges it.
integration: Supply agenda days, participant streams and join/leave callbacks. Keep selected meeting separate from the joined session.
Media callbacks resolve after host state changes succeed; failures preserve the previous control state.
Notes remain scoped by meeting ID. Hosts own storage, permissions and transport; the offline room uses fictional, camera-off participants.
